h1: Veranda Lodge Hua Hin — beachfront bungalows where you wake up to the sea at a price you can reach
intro: In a Hua Hin full of five-figure luxury resorts, Veranda Lodge is the choice for travellers who actually want to sleep on the beach without paying a fortune. It is a low-rise boutique lodge right on the southern stretch of Hua Hin beach that heads toward Khao Takiab, with everything from deluxe rooms and garden bungalows to sea-view suites just steps from the sand. Prices start at around ฿2,800/night. It scores 8.3 from 27 reviews on Trip.com and around 8.1 from over 1,600 reviews on Booking.com.

Beachfront restaurant at Veranda Lodge Hua Hin right by the water

body.html: Veranda Lodge sits at 113 Petchkasem Road on the southern part of Hua Hin beach — the stretch where the sand quietens down as it heads toward Khao Takiab. Its clearest selling point is simply being truly beachfront, not just near the beach. The property is a cluster of low-rise buildings and standalone bungalows spread through a garden, so it feels more like a small seaside village than a single hotel block. Many guests say the charm is being able to walk a few steps from the room straight onto the sand, at a price well below the big-brand resorts in the same area.

There is a good spread of room types to suit different budgets. The entry-level Deluxe Room runs around 25 sqm — simple but comfortable. Stepping up, the Garden Bungalow and Premier Deluxe at around 40 sqm give you more space, while travellers who want a direct sea view need the Veranda on Sea or the 60 sqm Balcony Suite. Each room has its own colour scheme. Most reviews describe the rooms as clean with cold air-con and strong showers, though a minority report soft water pressure and furniture that is starting to show its age — worth checking at check-in.

"Booking the seaside bungalow was so worth it — you open the door and there's the sand and the sea right there. Breakfast at the beachfront restaurant watching the fishing boats was lovely, and the staff knew our faces from day one."

The heart of a stay here is the beachfront. The lodge has a private sandy beach with complimentary sun loungers and kayaks, plus an outdoor pool for anyone who prefers not to swim in the sea. The beachfront restaurant is what reviews mention most, especially the breakfast served while you look out over the water, and the seafood dinners. Dinner by the sea at sunset is the moment guests remember. There are occasional notes about inconsistent service at the restaurant, but the seaside setting tends to make up for it.

The honest weak point is the condition of the buildings. A fair number of reviews note that the exteriors and some parts of the lodge are showing their age — faded paint, some worn lounger mattresses. The pool is fairly small and partly shaded by surrounding trees, so it is not a big resort-style pool. Some guests mention cat smells in certain corners, since the lodge is pet-friendly. The owners have refurbished some rooms and buildings, but if you expect everything to feel brand new you may need to adjust expectations — what you are paying for here is the location and the atmosphere, not luxury.

The location is a sweet spot for travellers who want both beach and convenience. It is a roughly 10-minute walk to Market Village and about a 5-minute drive to the centre of Hua Hin and the night market. You are on the quieter southern end of the beach but never far from the action, and Wat Khao Takiab, with its monkeys and sea views from the hilltop, is only a few minutes away. The lodge scores 8.3 from 27 reviews on Trip.com, around 8.1 from over 1,600 reviews on Booking.com, and ranks among the top boutique stays in Hua Hin on TripAdvisor.

To be straight about it, Veranda Lodge is not a luxury resort and is not trying to be one. It is a beachfront lodge offering a seaside location at a price ordinary travellers can book. Expect around ฿2,800–฿3,800/night for standard rooms in regular season, rising over long weekends. It suits couples or families who want to sleep by the sea and eat breakfast with a sea view without paying five-star resort prices. If you need a big pool, brand-new rooms or a full suite of facilities, look at a higher-priced resort instead.

A tip from those who follow the reviews here: if your budget allows, book the Veranda on Sea or a seaside bungalow to get the most out of staying here, because the whole appeal is sleeping right on the sand. Inspect your room at check-in and ask to switch if anything is too worn. Travelling with a pet? Tell them in advance, as there is an extra fee of around ฿1,000/night. And book in June or September — Hua Hin's low season — for the cheapest rates.

honestSummary: Veranda Lodge is best for travellers who genuinely want to sleep on a Hua Hin beach at a price they can comfortably book — a seaside location, private beach, beachfront breakfast and friendly staff. Just accept that it is a lodge where some buildings show their age, the pool is small, and it is not five-star resort luxury.
honestChecks: If you expect a luxury resort with brand-new rooms and a big pool — this is an affordable beachfront lodge where some buildings are old and the pool is small → consider a higher-priced five-star beachfront resort instead.
If you want a sea view and to sleep right on the sand — entry-level rooms face the garden, not the sea → book the Veranda on Sea or a seaside bungalow to make the stay worthwhile.
If you are sensitive to animal smells or dislike a pet-friendly vibe — the lodge welcomes pets and some corners have cat odours → request a room away from the pet area when booking.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Veranda Lodge Hua Hin

faq.q: Where is Veranda Lodge Hua Hin and what is nearby?
faq.a: It sits at 113 Petchkasem Road on the southern Hua Hin beach heading toward Khao Takiab. It is about a 10-minute walk to Market Village, a 5-minute drive to central Hua Hin and the night market, around 7 minutes to Wat Khao Takiab, and 12 minutes to Hua Hin Airport.

faq.q: How much does Veranda Lodge Hua Hin cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿2,800/night for a Deluxe Room (~25 sqm). Premier Deluxe and Garden Bungalow run around ฿3,500–3,800, and direct sea-view rooms like Veranda on Sea around ฿4,800. Rates vary by date, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is Veranda Lodge Hua Hin really beachfront?
faq.a: Yes. The lodge is right on the southern Hua Hin beach with a private sandy beach, free sun loungers and complimentary kayaks. You can walk from the room onto the sand in a few steps. The Veranda on Sea rooms and seaside bungalows are the most popular for a direct sea view.

faq.q: Are the rooms at Veranda Lodge Hua Hin old?
faq.a: It is a long-established lodge with some rooms refurbished. Some reviews note the exteriors and certain furniture are showing their age, and the pool is fairly small. We recommend inspecting your room at check-in and asking to switch if anything is too worn.

faq.q: Is Veranda Lodge Hua Hin pet-friendly?
faq.a: Yes. There is an extra fee of around ฿1,000/night. Flag it when booking and request a suitable room zone. Guests sensitive to animal smells should ask for a room away from the pet area, as some reviews mention cat odours in certain corners.

faq.q: When is the cheapest time to book?
faq.a: June and September are Hua Hin's low season with the cheapest rooms. Avoid long weekends and the New Year period when prices spike. Every platform offers a Free Cancellation option — choose it if your plans are not yet firm.
